answer: A farm that wants 250 keys as a result forfeits 250 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the orchard seed, the reef timing is verifiable from the juniper record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 592 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is cheap once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
